name: quiet-page
title: The note's icons at the window's right edge: going at the first key, staying through a pause, back with the hand on the mouse
description: Design 1 (principle 4), 5.5, 6.4. A note opened from the list shows Attach and Archive at the window's right edge, at 60%. The first key typed fades them (200 ms, standard); the pause that brings focus changes nothing about them (Slide: the list folds and the column glides, the icons stay at the edge); a deliberate movement of the mouse, 80 px over the text, brings them back (200 ms, standard), and only them: the list and the window's buttons stay away. Before this design the icons were in a gutter beside the column's first line, travelled with the column into focus, and came back only for a pointer within 64 px of them; the same scenario measures that.

setup.eval: (() => { const n = S.notes.find(n => !n.deleted && !n.archived); openD(n.id); document.querySelector('#d-text').focus(); return true; })()

movements.name: type
movements.description: A key typed in the note: the icons fade (200 ms) and nothing else moves; 600 ms later, with no key since, focus comes in (Slide: the list folds, the column glides) and the icons stay as they are. One movement: the app's own wait for the pause runs on the real clock, so stepping the first key alone would take in the pause too.

movements.name: hand
movements.description: The hand back on the mouse: 80 px of movement over the text. The icons come back; the list and the window's buttons do not.

between.eval: (() => { leaveFocus(); const n = S.notes.find(n => !n.deleted && !n.archived); openD(n.id); document.querySelector('#d-text').focus(); return true; })()
